---
title: "Reliability-based topology optimization (RBTO)"
toc: true
---

## Description

[Reliability-based topology optimization](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00158-010-0518-6)
(RBTO) searches for an optimal design while accounting for uncertainty in the
problem, such as random material properties. This tutorial walks through an
RBTO example with two materials: the Young's moduli are treated as log-normally
distributed random variables, and the objective is the mean plus two standard
deviations of the compliance.

## Setup

```{julia}
#| output: false
using ReliabilityOptimization, Test, ChainRulesCore
using TopOpt, Zygote, FiniteDifferences, Nonconvex
using Distributions, LinearAlgebra
```

## Problem definition

```{julia}
#| output: false
const v = 0.3 # Poisson's ratio
const densities = [0.0, 1.0] # for mass calc
const f = 1.0 # downward force
const nmats = 2
const V = 0.4 # volume fraction
const problemSize = (4, 4) # size of rectangular mesh
const elSize = (1.0, 1.0) # size of QUAD4 elements
# Point load cantilever problem to be solved
problem = PointLoadCantilever(problemSize, elSize, 1.0, v, f)
ncells = TopOpt.getncells(problem) # Number of elements in mesh
solver = FEASolver(DirectSolver, problem; xmin = 0.0)
filter = DensityFilterFun(solver; rmin = 3.0) # filter to avoid checkerboarding
comp = ComplianceFun(solver) # function that returns compliance
penalty = PowerPenaltyFun(3.0) # SIMP penalty
const avgEs = [1e-6, 0.5]
logEs = MvNormal(log.(avgEs), Matrix(Diagonal(abs.(log.(avgEs) * 0.1))))
```

## Random objective

The 'original' objective function takes the design variables and a random
sample of the Young's moduli as input. It is wrapped in a `RandomFunction` to
propagate the input uncertainty through the model.

```{julia}
#| output: false
function compObj(y, logEs)
    penalty1 = PowerPenaltyFun(3.0)
    interp1 = MaterialInterpolationFun(exp.(logEs), penalty1)
    x = tounit(MultiMaterialVariablesFun(y, nmats))
    _E = interp1(filter(x))
    dsd = comp(_E)
    return dsd
end
penalty2 = PowerPenaltyFun(1.0)
interp2 = MaterialInterpolationFun(densities, penalty2)
# wrap the original function in a RandomFunction struct
rf = RandomFunction(compObj, logEs; method = FORM(RIA()))
# initial homogeneous distribution of pseudo-densities
x0 = fill(V, ncells * (length(logEs) - 1))
# this returns a probability distribution of the objective at the current point
d = rf(x0)
```

## Optimization

```{julia}
constr = y -> begin
    _rhos = interp2(MultiMaterialVariablesFun(y, nmats))
    return sum(_rhos.x) / ncells - 0.4 # elements have unit volumes
end
function obj(x) # objective for the topology optimization problem
    dist = rf(x)
    return mean(dist)[1] + 2 * sqrt(cov(dist)[1, 1])
end

m = Model(obj) # create optimization model
addvar!(m, zeros(length(x0)), ones(length(x0))) # setup optimization variables
Nonconvex.add_ineq_constraint!(m, constr) # setup volume inequality constraint
@time r = Nonconvex.optimize(m, MMA87(), x0; options = MMAOptions())
```
